key_insight: A lightweight transfer-learning and hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász loss upgrade to BiSeNetV2 substantially improves weld seam segmentation robustness under strong reflections without increasing model complexity.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable real-time perception for construction welding robots, helping maintain seam tracking on shiny, harshly illuminated metal surfaces.
method: Fine-tuned a BiSeNetV2 backbone via transfer learning for seam segmentation.
Used a hybrid Cross-Entropy + Lovász loss to stabilize learning and improve boundary quality.
Kept FLOPs, parameters, and inference speed unchanged versus the baseline.
evidence_signal: The proposed method reached 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by +22.36 points over the OHEM baseline and recovering 96.33% of severe zero-IoU failures.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown on the reported dataset and conditions, so robustness on other weld types, sensor setups, and plant environments still needs validation.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
